settings.title: Built because we kept destroying stickers we loved.
settings.text:
KeepKase started at UC Berkeley. Ted had a MacBook covered in rare stickers — show tickets, brand collabs, memories from two years of college. Then he got a new laptop. The stickers were gone in 20 minutes. So was whatever they meant.

We spent six months prototyping a case that lets you preserve sticker layouts as physical objects. Two removable polycarbonate sheets. No adhesive ever touches your MacBook. Swap layouts whenever. Retire old sheets to your wall.

settings.heading: Three components. One system.
settings.text:
A hardshell PC border that clips onto your MacBook like any standard case. Two sheets of UV-stabilized polycarbonate — one inner, one outer — that sandwich your stickers between them.

No adhesive. No damage to anodization. No destruction when you want to change things up.

settings.heading: Your past should be portable.
settings.text: Retired sheets become framed objects. A year of college. A summer. A band era. They live on your wall instead of a landfill. We think that's worth building for.

settings.title: Ted
